Gen.3.15.lexical: אֵיבָה (342) 'enmity', fronted before אָשִׁית (qal yiqtol 1cs, 'I will set/put'): contrastive focus on enmity. זֶרַע (2233) collective singular 'seed/offspring', used for both sides. שׁוּף (7779) twice; rare (cf. Job 9:17, Ps 139:11 with disputed sense); meaning range 'strike / bruise / crush' vs a homonym or by-form near שׁאף 'snap at / lie in wait'. Same root in both clauses: lexical repetition should be preserved by one target verb.
Gen.3.15.syntactic: Four בֵּין phrases = two pairs (you/woman; your seed/her seed). הוּא 3ms agrees grammatically with masc. זֶרַע; it cannot grammatically refer to הָאִשָּׁה (fem). Emphatic pronouns הוּא … וְאַתָּה mark contrast between the two agents. יְשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ / תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵב: verb + pronominal object + accusative of the part affected ('strike you [on the] head', 'strike him [on the] heel').
Gen.3.15.discourse: Continues the address to the serpent begun in 3:14; setumah after the verse. Edition closes the serpent speech here.
Gen.3.15.textual: No variant in the pinned packet. Ancient versions are widely reported to differ (Greek masc. pronoun after a neuter noun; Latin tradition with a feminine pronoun; Greek verb 'watch/guard' for שׁוף). These are reception/translation facts, NOT verified in this run and not grounds for altering MT.
Gen.3.15.reception: Individual/messianic ('protevangelium'), Marian and collective-humanity readings are later interpretation; grammar neither requires nor excludes an individual referent.

Gen.3.16.lexical: עִצָּבוֹן (6093) 'pain/toil' — the SAME lexeme recurs in 3:17 for the man's labor (בְּעִצָּבוֹן תֹּאכְלֶנָּה) and later in 5:29; עֶצֶב (6089) in בְּעֶצֶב תֵּלְדִי is a related but different noun. הֵרֹן (2032), defectively spelled form of הֵרָיוֹן 'conception/pregnancy'. תְּשׁוּקָה (8669) rare (also 4:7; Song 7:11). מָשַׁל בְּ (4910) 'rule over'.
Gen.3.16.syntactic: הַרְבָּה אַרְבֶּה: infinitive absolute + finite, intensifying ('greatly increase'), not a numerical multiplier. עִצְּבוֹנֵךְ וְהֵרֹנֵךְ: two coordinated objects — literal 'your pain/toil and your pregnancy', or hendiadys 'your pain in pregnancy'. וְאֶל־אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ: verbless clause with fronted prepositional phrase; time reference supplied by context (future/descriptive). וְהוּא יִמְשָׁל־בָּךְ: qal yiqtol, predictive in this sentence-of-consequence context; jussive/normative reading is not marked morphologically.
Gen.3.16.discourse: Speaker implicit (YHWH God of 3:14); addressee shift marked by fronted אֶל־הָאִשָּׁה. 3:16 תְּשׁוּקָה + מָשַׁל בְּ is verbally echoed in 4:7 (תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ … תִּמְשָׁל־בּוֹ): the echo should be visible in each target language.
Gen.3.16.textual: No variant in the pinned packet. Greek is commonly reported to render the second noun as 'groaning' and תְּשׁוּקָה as 'turning'; NOT verified here.
Gen.3.16.reception: Desire as longing/attraction, dependence, or desire to control (by analogy with 4:7); 'rule' as description of a broken relation vs. a prescription — both interpretive layers, not settled by morphology.

findings.finding: 3:16 es 'él gobernará sobre ti' vs 4:7 es 'tú debes dominarlo' renders the same מָשַׁל בְּ with two verbs, while ko (다스리다) and en (rule over) keep the echo. Proposal: use dominar in both (3:16 'y él te dominará'), or gobernar in both. 'dominar' is idiomatic for 4:7 and attested in major Spanish usage for 3:16.
findings.strength: strongest concrete, low-risk wording point; editor choice of direction

findings.finding: The same noun is 'pain/고통/dolor' in 3:16 and 'painful toil/고된 수고/penoso trabajo' in 3:17; translations hide that the woman's and the man's sentences share a keyword. Text change not required (pain fits the childbirth context), but a note should state the shared lexeme and the 'toil' reading (parallel 'your toil and your pregnancies').
findings.strength: note-level; strongest objection to the hendiadys

findings.finding: en 3:16 'toward your husband' vs en 4:7 'Its desire is for you'. Both Hebrew clauses use אֶל + תְּשׁוּקָה; recommend one preposition in both (prefer 'toward', which keeps the directional אֶל and avoids reading 'for' as 'in favour of'). 4:7 belongs to another unit; recorded only as a consistency flag.

Current 'That offspring … that offspring' / '그 후손' / 'esa descendencia … la' is the most neutral option tested: it keeps grammatical agreement with זֶרַע, the הוּא/אַתָּה contrast and same-verb repetition without fixing individual vs collective. No change recommended.

strongest_objection_to_own_view: For 3:16 the hendiadys (which I keep) is an editorial fusion: the Hebrew coordinates two nouns, and the 3:17 reuse of עִצָּבוֹן supports 'toil'. A reader of 'pain in pregnancy' cannot see either fact. My answer: keep the readable selected text but require the note (F2); if the editor prioritises formal correspondence, the parallel option is the fallback. For 3:15 the strongest objection is that 'that offspring' is a demonstrative expansion of a bare pronoun.

final_opinion_ko: 두 절의 현행 채택문은 원문에 대한 오역이 없고, 대명사·동일 동사·중언법·미래 진술 처리 모두 방어 가능하다. 15절은 변경을 권하지 않는다. 16절은 스페인어에서 מָשַׁל בְּ가 4:7과 다른 동사로 옮겨져 평행이 깨지는 점(F1)이 가장 구체적 개선점이며, 17절과 공유하는 עִצָּבוֹן을 주석으로 드러낼 것(F2)과 영어 4:7 'for'/3:16 'toward' 통일(F3)을 권한다. 모두 편집 채택 전 GPT/Gemini 비교가 필요한 미채택 모델 의견이다.
